title: Kitchener's response to Province on southwest growth lands
subtitle: Regional Official Plan feedback, urban boundary, countryside line, net-zero and affordable housing goals, and a December 7 provincial deadline.
overview: Council held a special meeting to give the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing its position on the Regional Official Plan (ROPA 6). The Minister had asked for input within 45 days, and staff said December 7, 2023 was the deadline. Because two councillors would be away the following week, this was the last chance to respond as a full council.

Council supported the Minister's April 2023 decision, which added lands in southwest Kitchener to the urban area. An amendment extended the motion to a second parcel of non-protected countryside land, with the amendment carried {{vote:m3}}. The motion as amended also passed on a recorded vote {{vote:m2}}. It repeats Council's 2022 requests to the Region, including a 60% minimum intensification target and keeping any greenfield growth inside the countryside line. It also urges net-zero carbon design and affordable housing on the added lands.

This matters because it shapes where Kitchener may grow over the coming decade. It comes as the city works toward its pledge to build 35,000 homes by 2031. The Minister will decide what, if anything, changes. Council went in camera after the first session, and the minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council resolved to support the Minister's April 11, 2023 decision on ROPA 6, which added southwest Kitchener lands to the urban area, as part of its input to the Province {{vote:m2}}.

An amendment from Councillor Ioannidis extended the motion's support to a second parcel of non-protected countryside land in southwest Kitchener, replacing wording that limited support to lands inside the countryside line {{vote:m3}}.
Council urged that development on the subject lands be designed to net-zero carbon standards where possible and include affordable housing options.
The motion restates Council's 2022 requests that the Region support a minimum intensification target of at least 60% and confine any needed greenfield growth within the countryside line.
Council directed that the resolution be sent to the Premier, the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, the Region of Waterloo and all area municipalities.

debate: Developer representatives asked Council to include a second parcel near the Rosenberg area. They said it is already serviced, could deliver about 1,200 homes, and would help complete the Rosenberg secondary plan. They also asked for a deferral if no amendment was made.

Several delegates opposed the motion and asked for deferral. They cited little time for public engagement and no staff report, and said the Regional Official Plan already provides enough land. They also warned that added land could increase speculation and pressure on the countryside line, and that approved lots are not being built.
One delegate supported the countryside line but said Council should be strategic about how quickly it uses remaining land. Another asked for a clear strategy rather than one-off exceptions.

Councillors who backed the amendment said the 2022 Council position already sought these lands. They also said the Region's land needs assessment came before the extent of the housing supply shortage was known, and that servicing was already at the parcel's edge. They pointed to housing-start targets tied to provincial funding.

Staff said the Region, not the city, is responsible for land needs assessments, and a staff report could not be turned around in time. Staff also said the Planning Act allows subdivision approvals to lapse, but that tool could not be written into this motion.
